- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for potential reversal.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects in next period; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overshoot.  
- If true price deviates from 30-day moving average by >3%, model is biased; apply mean reversion correction: forecast = 30d MA + 0.5×(MA - last forecast).  
- For horizon > 14 days, model tends to lag true trend; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to account for delayed reaction.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.5, -0.5, +0.5), model often misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3 sentiment values to adjust forecast direction.
